newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, April 3.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Prime minister Romano Prodi paid a lightning visit to the rebel-held Albanian town of Gjirokaster for talks with his Albanian counterpart Bashkim Fino on preparing an Italian-led force to protect aid supplies (all).

* Relations between centre-left government and its key allies showed fresh signs of strain over the planned deployment of an Italian-led force to secure humanitarian relief to Albania. Prodi, addressing the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) after his ally the hard-left Communist Refoundation party opposed the mission, appealed for all sides to pull together for the sake of "higher national interests". The main centre-right opposition parties have pledged to support the security force (all).

* Hi-tech group Olivetti and France Telecome unveiled an alliance boosting the Italian company's telecoms strategy and giving the French group a significant foothold in Italy's market. The two companies said they signed a joint venture deal under which the French group would acquire 49 percent of Infostrada, a telecoms company set up by Olivetti and Bell Atlantic (all).
* Guido Rossi, chairman of state-controlled telecoms holding Stet, confirmed the group would take part together with AT&T Corp in a bid for the privatisation of cellular phones in Brazil (all).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian wage inflation stood at an annual 4.5 percent in January and 4.5 percent in February. Labour minister Tiziano Treu said the increase was in line with that of consumer prices. Istat also reported that the number of working hours in Italy lost as a result of industrial action and on other grounds rose 112.2 percent in 1996 to 13.5 million hours from 6.4 million in 1995 (all).
* Italian post Ente Poste Italiane can break even in three years either with government incentives, or through cutting 15,000 jobs or by increasing the cost of services by 20 percent (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
